reviews.text: Thank you for your feedback. We look forward to your continued support.

My cat, inherited from my late parents, has been receiving care here since 2018.

Originally, I took her to the Japan Animal Medical Center, but the two bus transfers or taxi rides with a large cat were difficult, and the frequent doctor transfers at such a large hospital were a bit of a drawback.

This hospital is within walking distance, so samples can be delivered quickly, and she can receive thorough care from the same doctor. Therefore, I now primarily use this hospital, only going to the aforementioned hospital for after-hours appointments.

January 2026:
I'm reducing the star rating and adding this note due to frequent issues with the reception staff's service.

・Even though I verbally stated that the urine sample contained UPC, and it was also written on the attached form, it was overlooked, and the bill was calculated based on the cheaper general test fee. It was corrected later.

While mistakes are understandable (though it's a matter of life and health, so it's hard to say that), I felt the lack of a proper apology after pointing it out was insincere.


January 2026:
I'm reducing the star rating and adding this note due to recent issues with the reception staff's service.

- After vomiting four times in a row, I called to inquire about an available gastrointestinal ultrasound appointment for that day. The response was a dismissive, almost threatening tone, saying, "You must first have a consultation," stating something I already knew in a condescending manner.

The implication was clearly, "You may not know this, but this is our policy."

Couldn't they have simply said, "I'll check with the doctor"?

It felt like they were trying to use my anxiety to create a sense of superiority.

It seems there are one or two staff members with an excessive sense of entitlement.

- The Gaster tablets (prescribed without issue) given to me during the vomiting visit didn't agree with my child, resulting in nearly a week of watery diarrhea.

I understand that Gaster, unlike antibiotics, can be stopped once the vomiting subsides, but I was told at the reception to "finish the entire 5-day supply," which contributed to my feeling that I had to administer it properly.

I thought I might have misheard, but later I heard the same thing said to someone else regarding some kind of medication, asking them to "please finish the entire course."

However, since the receptionist isn't a doctor, shouldn't she just hand over the medication without giving any instructions?

She should draw a line and say, "Please take the medication exactly as instructed by your doctor regarding dosage and frequency," and should have no authority whatsoever to delve into medical or pharmaceutical matters, and should refrain from giving any instructions.


On the day when my child had watery diarrhea 20 times and was suffering terribly, I went to the clinic first thing after it opened and asked for triage, but she responded in a condescending, defiant tone, saying, "Please make an appointment for 9:45, the earliest time, and we'll do triage then."

No, triage doesn't mean appointment order! I said, but she just replied, "Is that so?" as if it were someone else's problem.

When I said I would take my child somewhere else that day, she again responded in a haughty, arrogant tone with just, "Understood," and ended the conversation.

They showed absolutely no empathy for my life-or-death situation, so I decided to move my base of operations to my more convenient home in Shinjuku Ward and never ask for their help again! I headed to a large hospital.

Whether they were receptionists or not, they lacked any sense of professionalism or human warmth.


After my visit to the large hospital, I felt better and was instructed to return here for IV treatments, so I went back.

When I made the appointment, I mentioned the IV medications A and B specified by the large hospital, and the doctor confidently repeated, "A and B, understood."

However, when I arrived at the scheduled time, it turned out they didn't have B, and the doctor apologized profusely.

If they had checked the availability at the time of booking, I wouldn't have wasted my trip, and the treatment could have progressed smoothly.

Fortunately, the severe symptoms were starting to subside, but it was past the time when other hospitals were closed. What would have happened if this had been a life-sustaining medication?

This is just what I can remember; there are countless other examples.

Overall, I feel a disconnect in the conversation, similar to interacting with a poorly performing AI.

I get the impression that your work motive isn't "to help people," but rather "to act like someone with authority and knowledge," but "without wanting to do more work than necessary."

In this industry, miscommunication can be life-threatening.

I would like to strongly urge you to once again provide strict guidance to ensure that only doctors make judgments and give instructions, and that you focus solely on being a messenger, without letting your pride or personal judgment interfere.

I have been under your care for about 25 years.
I am truly grateful to the doctors for their efforts, which allowed my golden retriever to live to the age of 17, and for the mixed-breed rescue dog I am currently looking after to remain healthy at over 14 despite a recurrence of cancer.
They took very good care of me while I was in hospital, and they also worked in cooperation with the university hospital, always explaining things to me carefully, so I am receiving the best medical care.
I felt I don't have many opportunities to express my gratitude on a daily basis, so I decided to write here. I hope you will continue to support me in the future.

My beloved cat is 13 years old, one of two twins.

Six months ago, one of them passed away.

Despite being twins, one was often ill, and at 1.5 years old, her life seemed to be ending. The head veterinarian here performed surgery, and thankfully, her life was saved.

After that, she suffered from various illnesses and received care here, but her kidney failure worsened, and she eventually became unable to eat and was hospitalized.

Every time I visited, the head veterinarian and all the other doctors explained her condition in detail, and the nurses were also very kind.

My cat is very shy, but it seemed she was responding to the staff's words, which showed how warmly they were caring for her.

I was told she didn't have long to live, and wanting her to spend her last moments with our family and her twin, I stopped treatment and brought her home. However, making that decision required a lot of resolve, and it took a long time, but they understood my feelings and waited patiently.

Five days after being discharged from the hospital, our beloved cat passed away, surrounded by her family and twin siblings.

We are incredibly lonely and sad, but we feel that our decision to bring her home was the right one. We are deeply grateful to the head veterinarian, doctors, nurses, and staff who were so understanding and supportive of us pet owners.

Thank you so much.

I wanted to comment immediately on how wonderful this hospital is, but remembering our cat brought up so many emotions that I couldn't write for a while.

Our other twin sibling seems healthy for now, and we continue to receive care for their health checkups.

We look forward to your continued support.
Thank you very much for your feedback. We look forward to your continued support.
I apologize if there are any shortcomings.

My beloved dog was cared for there for 15 and a half years. Every veterinarian was incredibly thorough in their examinations, listening attentively to what I had to say as a pet owner, which made me feel at ease. My dog ​​suddenly became ill, and I rushed to the emergency room (they're open 24 hours a day). The head veterinarian, who had gone home, came to see my dog. At that point, his blood pressure couldn't be measured, and blood couldn't be drawn for tests, but he very kindly explained the situation. He said that sometimes dogs recover, but even if they seem healthy, their internal organs are aging, and they might pass away that night.
He gave me time to prepare myself, and I was able to call my daughter, who lives a little distance away.
An hour after returning home, my dog ​​passed away surrounded by my family, and I was able to face that moment calmly.
I am so grateful for the love and care everyone gave my dog ​​for 15 and a half years; it's a wonderful hospital.
Thank you very much for your feedback.
It's a good hospital where you can feel safe with any doctor. However, because they are so thorough, the cost can be high if they do a lot of tests.
Thank you for your rating. We will continue to work hard to receive positive reviews.
I'm always very satisfied with the kind and helpful service I receive.

We've been going to this clinic for a long time, and they've always treated our pets with the same care and attention. They noticed our pet's illness and responded immediately. The trustworthy doctor and nurses are very sincere, so it's a hospital where you can feel at ease consulting with them.

Thank you for your feedback.

We look forward to your continued support.
Thank you very much for your feedback. We look forward to your continued support.

I've been taking my rabbit to this clinic for checkups. The female veterinarian is very kind and attentive, and I always feel at ease leaving my rabbit in her care. She explains everything thoroughly, so as a pet owner, I trust this hospital.

Dr. Hata is very experienced, kind, caring, and knowledgeable.  He helped us with the paperwork for the AQS (Animal Quarantine Service) to bring our puppy home to the U.S.

We were visiting Japan from California and my daughter fell in love with a puppy that she really wanted to bring home to the U.S.A.  The pet shop vets said they did not know how to write a health certificate in English.  Their vets asked us to provide an English form.  I had no idea what form to provide and where I would get it from!

I panicked and started looking around for other hospitals that had English-speaking vets.  I tried one other hospital but it was hard getting to a nurse that spoke English and she was not as quick to respond, nor was she as thorough about checking on our status and needs for our puppy export/import paperwork.

Then I found the Igusa Animal Hospital website.  Unlike some of the other hospitals that offered an English-speaking vet, Igusa actually had an email contact. I wrote to Dr. Hata in English and he responded immediately.  Upon hearing of our timeline and desired return flight date, he was concerned about the deadline and immediately had me fill out a form on the Igusa website that had very thorough details needed for the AQS inspection.  The fact that his website was so prepared was very impressive!.  He then wrote up a preliminary draft of the health certificate and sent it to me so we could send it to the AQS for approval and to help confirm if any information was missing so that he could be sure that we would pass inspection.  He did all this even before we had gone to see him because he was so concerned about our deadline!

While writing the preliminary health certificate, he realized that our puppy was really young and small.  He was very concerned and in the most thoughtful way possible, voiced his concerns about the puppy traveling in cargo.  I assured him that the puppy would be traveling in the cabin with a person, by flying on an American airline.  Japanese airlines only allow pets in cargo and there is the chance of death so we purposefully found an American airline that met all of our requirements.  Dr.  Hata was very relieved to hear that and then further voiced his concerns about our puppy getting the 3rd mixed vaccine two days before the flight and so close to the rabies vaccine.  He sent us an information guide about vaccine spacing and rare, but possible side effects, etc.  Based on his concerns, I told him we could skip the 3rd mixed vaccine until after the puppy was in the United States.  Once again, he was very relieved to hear that.  From these interactions, I was very touched by how caring Dr. Hata was.

Shortly after, our Japanese friend rebooked us with an English-speaking vet from the pet shop clinic for the rabies vaccine (which would now be our last vaccine in Japan) and a health exam.  We went to get the rabies vaccine and exam and the English-speaking vet was able to give us an English health certificate.  But since I wanted to pay Dr. Hata for his efforts, and I had more confidence in him, we went to Dr. Hata two days after for another health exam.  After inspecting our puppy, he gave us the final health certificate.

Once again, I was very impressed!  Dr. Hata's health certificate documented all the vaccines that my puppy had, all the info that were asked in the AQS application form, and included extra health statements that I felt were needed to ensure a smooth and successful inspection at the AQS and to provide assurance to the airline we were boarding.  These were details that were not on the pet shop vet's health certificate.  They may not have been necessary to pass the AQS inspection, but I felt more confident and re-assured with these extra details in Dr. Hata's certificate.

A few days later, we passed the AQS inspection.  Our puppy is now home with us in California!  Thank you so much, Dr. Hata for helping us understand the paperwork and the AQS application process better!  Thank you for being so caring and voicing your concerns for the pet!
Thank you very much for your feedback. We look forward to your continued support.
The veterinarian is very kind and explains things thoroughly, so I feel confident leaving my pet in their care.
